evidence: Cic. Fam. 6.1.4: ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.3.5: quem tamen ego praestāre nōn poteram (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To vouch for, warrant, take upon oneself: to be liable for a loss is damnum praestāre. Its other common senses are to excel, to show, and to perform (see perform).

terms.gloss: liable, answerable (to a penalty, a law, a person)
evidence: Plaut. Truc. 4.3.61: ego tibi mē obnoxium esse fateor culpae compotem (Lewis & Short)
Dig. 11.3.14: ego lēge Aquīliā obnoxius sum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Subject to punishment, liable; then subject, submissive, beholden in general. It never means “obnoxious”.

phrases.latin: simus eā mente ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus
phrases.english: let us be of a mind to think that in life we must answer for nothing but our own wrongdoing
